## B.7.4 Preparation

1. Ensure that all completion sub-assemblies are torqued, measured, drifted, and pressure tested prior to running the completion.
2. If the Y-Tool sub assembly is a standard type, with Blanking Plug, then determine if it is required to run the completion with the Blanking Plug installed or removed. The plug can be removed or set in the Y-Tool assembly on deck using Stem Bar, Spang Jars, and the pulling and running tools specified in the correct Blanking Plug SOP.

3. If the Y-Tool assembly includes a Top Nipple profile for a Standing Valve, then determine if it is required to run the completion with the Standing Valve installed or removed. The plug can be removed or set in the Y-Tool assembly on deck using Stem Bar, Spang Jars and the pulling and running tools specified in the correct Standing Valve SOP.
4. Stroke open the Teleswivel to mid-stroke position. Normally 7.5 in stroke open for mid position (15 in full stroke).
5. Measure (tally) the make up lengths of all the bypass tubing and ESP sections.
6. Refer to Appendix 1 to create a bypass tubing space out diagram.
7. Mark the pick up order of the bypass tubing as per the space out diagram.
8. Referring to the space out diagram, determine where the ESP connections will lie relative to the bypass tubing alongside. Mark the bypass joints showing where the ESP connections will lie when alongside.
9. Fit the WEG to the first joint of bypass tubing using wrenches.
10. Locate the Pothead on the upper motor. Use a bypass clamp to establish the position of the bypass tubing relative to the Pothead. Refer to .
11. Draw a vertical line down the full length of the motor to mark the position of the bypass tubing. If there is more than one motor section in the string, use the head and base bolt patterns to continue the line for the bypass tubing position down the length of each motor section.
12. If there are additional lines to be run past the ESP, for example a gauge pressure discharge line, and/or chemical injection lines, then use the bypass clamp cable clips to determine where these will be positioned. The position of MLE and control lines secured by the clamp will depend on the clamp type, and the application. Make any further markings required on the ESP units to aid positioning of these lines during the assembly.

<!-- image -->

13. If applicable, fit the gauge to base of the lower motor. If the gauge has a pressure discharge, or Remote Sub line then ensure the gauge is correctly aligned on the motor, for the position of the line.
14. Fit the motor base plug (if included) to the bottom of the motor, or gauge (if included) using wrenches.

## B.7.5 ESP Bypass Assembly

1. Fit the swivel lift nubbin to the first bypass joint. Pick up the assembly with the tugger / air winch. Position over the well and RIH.
2. Position the ESP worktable over the well. Fit the safety clamp to the bypass tubing and torque to 200 ft.lbf. Land on the ESP worktable.
3. Remove the swivel lift nubbin and fit to the next bypass tubing joint. Pick up the joint with the tugger / air winch and make up to the assembly using wrenches.
4. Pick up to remove the safety clamp. POOH until the mark on the bypass tubing for the bottom of the motor is at working height.
5. Fit the lifting clamp to the ESP motor and pick up with the elevators.
6. Manoeuvre motor over the well. If applicable make up the pressure discharge line or remote sub line to the gauge.

<!-- image -->

## Note

If a pressure discharge line is fitted to the gauge, it should be pressure tested at this point.

7. Position the motor alongside the bypass tubing and orientate such that the vertical line drawn on the motor is in line with the bypass tubing. Adjust the height of the motor such that the base is in line with the marking made on the bypass tubing.
8. Referring to SOP 100476874, fit a bypass clamp to the base of the motor (or motor base plug if fitted). Securing control lines if applicable.
9. Slowly RIH with the assembly servicing the motor as required.
10. Land the motor on the ESP worktable / stovepipe.
11. Pick up and make up the next section of ESP. Pick up to remove lifting clamp. Referring to SOP 100476874, fit a bypass clamp to the base of the ESP unit, securing lines if applicable.

## Private

12. RIH with the assembly to the top of the bypass tubing joint. Fit the safety clamp to the bypass tubing.
13. Remove the swivel lift nubbin. Pick up the next section of bypass tubing with the tugger / air winch, and make up with wrenches. Remove safety clamp.
14. Continue to RIH with the assembly making up ESP sections and bypass tubing joints as required. As each unit is added, ensure the bypass tubing has not slipped by confirming the ESP make up points match the markings made on the bypass tubing.
15. Once the Protectors have been fitted tie in the MLE and perform electrical tests. Refer to SOP 100476874 to fit a bypass clamp to each ESP neck, securing MLE cable and any additional lines.

<!-- image -->

## Note

A bypass clamp should not be fitted directly below the pump intake. If a bolt on intake is used, a clamp can be fitted above the intake, however if the intake is integral, then the clamp should be omitted.

16. Once all the ESP units and bypass tubing joints have been made up, continue to RIH and land the pump lifting clamp on the ESP worktable / stovepipe.
17. If applicable make up the pressure discharge sub, or remote sub to the top of the pump observing correct alignment for the position of the line.
18. Pick up the Y-Tool sub assembly with the elevators. Position the discharge head over ESP assembly. Align the Y-Tool sub assembly so that the teleswivel is in alignment with the bypass tubing.
19. Slowly lower the Y-Tool assembly and make up the discharge head to the top of the ESP assembly.
20. Pick up the assembly to remove the ESP lifting clamp.
21. Slowly lower the assembly so that the teleswivel is at working height. Fit the safety clamp to the bypass tubing and torque to 200 ft.lbf. Remove the lifting nubbin and make up the teleswivel to the bypass tubing. Tighten the teleswivel sleeve and secure lock ring.
22. POOH to the discharge head. If applicable terminate pressure discharge or remote sub line.
23. Referring to SOP 100476874, fit a bypass clamp to the discharge head, securing lines if applicable.

## Private

24. Slowly RIH with the assembly to the Y-Tool. Secure the MLE in the cable clip at one side of the Y- Tool. If applicable, secure control lines in cable clip at opposite side of Y-Tool.
25. Slowly RIH with the assembly and set the slips on the handling sub.

## B.7.6 Constructing a Bypass Space Out Drawing

1. Use to sketch the ESP units of the string, including MultiSensor, Pressure Discharge Sub or Remote Sensor etc.
2. Mark on the lengths, of the pump sub, and all the ESP units. Assume the base of the Y-Tool to be depth 0.00 and working from top down, add up the lengths of the ESP string, noting each flange or make up point as a depth from 0.00. See .
3. Add the length of the Teleswivel at mid stroke to the sketch.
4. Working from the Teleswivel down, add lengths of bypass tubing to the sketch. As each length is added, calculate the depth relative to 0.00 at the make up point.
5. It is recommend that the bypass tubing extend at least 10 ft below the base of the ESP. This should be discussed with the client in case of special requirements.
6. Calculate where each ESP flange (make up point) will lie with respect to the bypass tubing joints alongside, and note on the drawing. See finished example in Figure B-21.

## C Maximus

## C.1 Introduction

The standard Maximus equipment installation is almost identical to other equipment. The exceptions are:

- The ProMotor is factory-filled at the manufacturing plant and does not require oil servicing at the wellsite.
- Maximus protectors are factory-filled and factory-shimmed, no oil filling or shimming measurements are required at the wellsite because they arrive to the wellsite ready to plug-and-play.
- The MaxLok ESP motor pothead design eliminates the need for taping pothead electrical connections.

The Trident motor head is available for high amperage and extreme reliability requirements such as subsea installations. The Trident motor head is compatible with the Trident MLE which has three individual conductors and potheads.

Detailed specifications are available in the Product Bulletins REDA Maximus Motors (InTouch Content ID 4206720) and Protectors (InTouch Content ID 4206743) for internal reference and in Product data sheets for external reference.

## C.3 Wellsite Procedures

## C.3.1 General Notes on MaxJoints and Shipping Caps

The following general notes are applicable to all joints between Maximus motors, protectors and ProMotors, which are known as MaxJoints.

1. The MaxJoint allows making up a flange without trapping air or loss of required oil. Therefore, Maximus motors, protectors and ProMotors do not normally require field refilling upon installation unless oil is lost.
2. A compensating shipping cap is used on the head of all Maximus motors, protectors and ProMotors, except for a few cases where it is not required. For example, 400 series UT protectors with a bag on top do not require a compensating shipping cap because the bag acts as a compensator and another protector cannot be mated to it. The compensating shipping cap compensates for the oil thermal expansion and contraction during the storage and transportation of the units.

Figure C-2: Compensating shipping cap on UT motor

<!-- image -->

3. On receipt of the unit (motor, protector or ProMotor) at the wellsite inspect the unit and the shipping box, or container for signs of oil leakage. It is normal for residual oil to drain from between the housing and the bag of the compensating shipping. However, if a significant amount of oil has leaked from other locations on the unit, it needs to be refilled according to the oil-filling procedures. Refer to the standard wellsite procedures in the unless specified otherwise.
4. When lifting a unit equipped with a compensation shipping cap, a Spreader Lifting Chain (100367280) must be used to lift Maximus Equipment. In case of emergency, if the Spreader Lifting Chain is not available, two normal chains (0902437) can be connected together on the clamp with a 3/4-in link (0902262) to make a chain long enough to clear the compensating shipping cap. In cases where the 3/4-in link is not available, then three normal chains (0902437) can be connected together to make a chain long enough to clear the compensating shipping cap.

<!-- image -->

Potential Severity:

Major

Potential Loss:

Assets, Personnel

Hazard Category:

Land transport

The compensating shipping cap must not be used as a lifting point for lifting the unit because it can break and let the equipment fall, endangering personnel and equipment.

## Private

5. If the conventional shipping cap on the equipment base is difficult to remove because of a partial vacuum. The drain-and-fill valve on the shipping cap may be loosened to relieve the vacuum.
6. After the shipping cap has been removed from a base and the oil contained within the shipping cap has drained, the oil communication valve and the shaft seal in the base should prevent continued loss of oil. If oil continues to drain and more oil is lost than the compensating shipping cap on the head of the unit can make up, the unit may need to be refilled as discussed by the following.
7. When the compensating shipping cap is removed from the head, the head should be overflowing with oil. Watch the oil level for a few minutes and wait for any bubbles in the system to rise to the surface. The length of time required for this will vary according to equipment type, length and temperature. If the oil level falls more than 0.5 in. (13 mm) or bubbles larger than 0.5 in (13 mm) diameter continue to rise, the unit may not be properly filled with oil or may have lost oil. It should be refilled with the proper oil per the standard wellsite procedures, in the same manner as Dominator motors or Modular protectors. If the oil level continues to fall, check for a leaking drain-and-fill valve or vent plug or reject the unit.
8. After removing a compensating shipping cap, it should be cared for and returned for salvage or reuse. Set the compensating shipping cap upside down to minimize oil loss and avoid contamination. Protect it by installing the shipping cap and gasket removed from the base of the unit above it.
9. If oil is displaced, lowering the oil level more than 0.12 in (3 mm) below the flange face, while preparing to make up a flange connection (checking shaft rotation, aligning splines, etc.), top it off by pouring more of the proper oil into the head. Refer to the oil specification for the equipment.
10. When a flange is made up, an actuator ring in the head of the lower unit lifts the oil communication valve in the base of the unit above it to establish communication. Make sure the actuator ring is present in the head of the lower unit. Also avoid any damage to the communication valve in the base of the upper unit.
11. When a flange is made up, excess oil will be displaced from the head. If the joint is reopened, the head must be refilled with oil before making it up again. Otherwise, air will be trapped in the joint.

Refer to Table C-3 for Maximus compensating shipping caps and hardware part numbers. Refer to the ALFORM-D connection tables (InTouch ID: 3255850) for a complete list of O-ring part numbers, coupling and bolt torque information.

## C.3.3 Installation of Phoenix Gauge

The Phoenix gauge can be installed onto the Gauge-Ready-Base (GRB) motors at the wellsite. Installation of the gauge can also be done in the shop. The gauge can be installed either vertically or horizontally. When the lower shipping cap is taken off for gauge installation, the check valve inside the base prevents the oil from leaking out off the motor. After the gauge is installed, only the small space between the base and the gauge needs to be filled. The motor itself does not need to be refilled.

Figure C-3: Gauge Ready Base (GRB) in Maximus S and LT motors

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

Figure C-4: Maximus LT - GRB Motor Connected to a Phoenix Select Gauge

<!-- image -->

## Note

There are two drain-and-fill valves in the GRB, marked with 'G' for communication to gauge, and 'M' for communication to motor.

Section Appendix C.3.3.1: Installing Gauge Vertically and Appendix C.3.3.2: Installing Gauge Horizontally describe the gauge installation options.

## C.3.3.1 Installing Gauge Vertically

1. Remove the vent plug from the GRB to relieve the vacuum inside the base, so that the cap can be easily removed.
2. Remove the shipping cap from the GRB.
3. Uncoil the I-wire and thermocouple wires from inside of the GRB.
4. Lift the gauge close to the base.
5. Connect the boots of the I-wire and the thermocouple wires to the corresponding terminals in the gauge head.
6. Install the gauge onto the base and fasten it to the base with the specified washers and bolts.

## Private

7. Tighten the bolts with torque setting refer to the DME manual for that particular equipment.
8. Fill the space between the base and the gauge by pumping oil into the D and F valve marked with 'G' until oil runs clear out off the vent hole.
9. Install plugs into the vent holes and drain-and-fill valves with new lead gaskets.

<!-- image -->

## Note

Make sure the vent plugs are torqued to 15 ft-lbf and the drain-and-fill valves are torqued to 35 ft-lbf.

## C.3.3.2 Installing Gauge Horizontally

1. Remove the vent plug from the GRB to relieve the vacuum inside the base, so that the cap can be easily removed.
2. Remove the shipping cap from the GRB.
3. Uncoil the I-wire and thermocouple wires from inside of the GRB.
4. Lift the gauge close to the base.
5. Connect the boots of the I-wire and the thermocouple wires to the corresponding terminals in the gauge head.
6. Install the gauge onto the base and fasten it to the base with the specified washers and bolts.
7. Tighten the bolts with torque setting refer to the DME manual for that particular equipment.
8. Roll the motor so that the vent hole in the base is pointing up.
9. Fill the space between the base and the gauge by pumping oil into the D and F valve marked with 'G' until oil runs out off the vent hole. Alternatively, oil may be poured into the vent hole until it overflows.
10. Install plugs into the vent holes and drain-and-fill valves with new lead gaskets.

<!-- image -->

## Note

Make sure the vent plugs are torqued to 15 ft-lbf and the drain-and-fill valves are torqued to 35 ft-lbf.

## C.3.4 Motor Installation

## C.3.4.1 Installation of Single Section Motor and Single Section ProMotor

<!-- image -->

Potential Severity:

Light

Potential Loss:

Information

Hazard Category:

Machinery equipment hand tools

Caution

Before proceeding, read and follow section Appendix C.3.1: General Notes on MaxJoints and Shipping Caps.

To install a single section motor or single section ProMotor, perform the following steps:

1. Raise the S (single section) motor (or S ProMotor throughout this section) over the wellhead and remove the tail clamp before lowering it into the wellhead.
2. Lower the S motor into the wellhead until the clamp rests on the work table. While lowering it, the plugs and drain-and-fill valves in the base and the head should be inspected for signs of leakage.
- a. Tighten the valve body to 35 lbf-ft.
- b. Tighten the vent plug in the valve to 15 lbf-ft.

<!-- image -->

## Note

If the clamp prevents access to the head drain-and-fill valve, check it later after the clamp has been removed.

3. Remove the compensating shipping cap from the motor head. Check for free shaft rotation.
4. It is now ready to receive the next piece of the string, (e.g., protector, intake, gas device or pump). Place a clean spare conventional shipping cap on the head with two screws to prevent contamination while preparing the next piece.

## C.3.4.2 Installation of Lower Tandem motor

<!-- image -->

Potential Severity:

Light

Potential Loss:

Information

Hazard Category:

Caution

Before proceeding, read and follow the general notes above on MaxJoints and compensating shipping caps.

To install a lower tandem Maximus motor, perform the following steps:

1. Raise the LT motor over the wellhead and remove the tail clamp before lowering it into the wellhead.
2. While lowering the LT motor, the plugs and drain-and-fill valves in the base and the head should be inspected for signs of leakage.
- a. Tighten the valve body to 35 lbf-ft.
- b. Tighten the vent plug in the valve to 15 lbf-ft.

<!-- image -->

## Note

If the clamp prevents access to the head drain-and-fill valve, check it later after the clamp has been removed.

3. Lower the LT motor into the wellhead until the head clamp is approximately 18 in from the top of the work table.

<!-- image -->

## Note

For use in temperatures below 5 degF (-15 degC), the hydraulic motor jacks should be filled with a low temperature oil, such as Exxon Univis HV113 (B044780). The oil normally supplied with the jacks may become too viscous for the jacks to operate.

4. Slide the motor jack assembly (44826) into position on the work table. Ensure that both hydraulic jacks are in their retracted position.
5. Lower the motor into the wellhead until the clamp rests in the cradle on top of the jacks.
6. Remove the compensating shipping cap from the motor head.

## Private

7. Check for free shaft rotation.
8. It is now ready to receive the next piece of the string (e.g., CT motor, UT motor or UT ProMotor). Place a clean spare conventional shipping cap on the head with two screws to prevent contamination while preparing the next piece.

## C.3.4.3 Installation of CT Motor, UT Motor or UT ProMotor

<!-- image -->

Potential Severity:

Light

Information

## Caution

Before proceeding, read and follow the general notes above on MaxJoints and compensating shipping caps.

To install CT/UT Motors (CT motor, UT Motor or UT ProMotor) perform the following steps:

1. Raise the CT/UT Motor over the wellhead. Remove the tail clamp and the lower shipping cap.
2. Use the spline alignment tool listed in Table C-4 to align the flange
- a. Insert the male end of the alignment tool into the coupling on the LT shaft.
- b. Turn the shaft until the LT alignment stud enters the hole in the tool.
- c. Remove the tool without rotating the shaft.
- d. Place the female end of the tool over UT shaft.
- e. Turn the shaft until the tool pin enters the correct bolt hole in the UT flange for the LT alignment stud, adjacent to the alignment groove on the flange OD.
- f. Remove the tool without rotating the shaft.

3. Select the correct O-ring(s) from Table C-3 (456 Series uses 996058, 562 Series uses 1018761). Refer to the ALFORM-D connection tables (InTouch ID: 3255850) for a complete list of torque specifications. Lubricate the O-ring with Dow Corning Lubricant (0553420). Remove old O-ring and carefully install the new one into the correct position.

<!-- image -->

Potential Severity:

Light

Potential Loss:

Assets, Process

Hazard Category:

Machinery equipment hand tools

Caution

It is important when connecting tandem motors that the rig is centered over the wellbore and that the traveling blocks are not swaying. In strong wind conditions, it may be necessary to have someone at the monkey board holding the blocks stationary, centered over the wellhead. Alternatively, this can be done from the floor with a rope or cable around the unit and tied back to the rig.

4. Inspect the terminal pins and insulators to ensure they are not bent or broken.
- a. Have the rig operator lower the CT/UT Motor approximately 4- to 6-in above the LT Motor.
- b. Pump both jacks simultaneously to slowly raise the LT Motor and engage the coupling.

Make sure the alignment pin slides into the respective hole and that the motor terminals are properly engaged.

<!-- image -->

Potential Severity:

Light

Potential Loss:

Assets

Hazard Category:

Electrical

Caution

Use care not to damage the terminal insulators or O-rings.

5. Install the bolts and lock washers. The torque specifications for 456 and 562 Series is 26 lbf-ft. Refer to the ALFORM-D connection tables (InTouch ID: 3255850) for a complete list of torque specifications.
6. Lower the CT/UT Motor into the wellhead until the clamps rest on the work table. While lowering the motor, each drain-and-fill valve and protector vent plug should be inspected for signs of leakage.
- a. Tighten the valve body to 35 lbf-ft.
- b. Tighten the vent plug in the valve to 15 lbf-ft.
7. Remove the shipping cap from the motor (or protector of a ProMotor) head and check rotation.

## Private

8. It is now ready to receive the next piece of string (e.g., protector, intake, gas device, pump). Place a clean spare conventional shipping cap on the head with two screws to prevent contamination while preparing the next piece.

## C.3.4.4 Installation of UT Motor with Trident Motor Head

Currently, two types of Trident UT motors are available the 738 Maximus motor (Trident-300) and 562 Maximus motor (Trident-400).

1. Lower UT motor and set the lifting clamp on to the hydraulic jack cradles and plate which are set in position on the top of the work table, remove spreader bar shackles from UT clamps.

<!-- image -->

## Note

Ensure the hole covers are installed around the shroud to eliminate any debris/tooling falling into the shroud and capsule.

2. Fit the appropriate clamp onto the upper part of the compensating shipping cap (below shoulder on motor head).

<!-- image -->

## Note

The standard 3/8-in plug (on the side of the head) at the top of the compensation shipping cap must be removed before attempting to dissemble the shipping cap from the ESP section. A vacuum may be present and it's possible that the ESP section can be picked up if the unit is not allowed to equalize.

3. Secure the shackles of the spreader bar onto the friction clamp.
4. Remove compensating shipping cap bolts from the flange and prepare to remove the compensating shipping cap.

<!-- image -->

## Note

Make sure there is a spare 5 gallon plastic oil-bucket to catch the excess oil from the compensating shipping cap when remove it from the UT motor.

5. Slowly pick up compensating shipping cap and fit lower flange cap, lay equipment off to the side of the work area.

## Private

## C.3.5 Protector Installation

By virtue of MaxJoint technology, Maximus protectors are ready for installation upon arrival at the wellsite. With no oil servicing required, the only procedure remaining at wellsite is to plug-and-play the motor and protector.

The screws at the lower and upper ends of Maximus protector shafts are shimmed by manufacturing to a very tight tolerance, ±0.003 in. Therefore, it is not necessary to take any shimming measurements at the wellsite.

## C.3.5.1 Tandem Maximus Protectors

In tandem Maximus protector applications, additional shims are required between the lower and upper protector due to thermal expansion. The additional shims should be calculated and prepared in the ART Center prior to the installation. If this is not possible, the shims calculation must be done in the field.

The additional shims for each tandem protector application are calculated by considering the well fluid temperature at pump setting depth (BHT), lower protector make-up length and material. The formulas for calculating the additional shims are listed in section Appendix C.3.5.2: Tandem Maximus Protector Shimming Calculations.

<!-- image -->

## Note: Communicate shimming requirements

The Application Engineer must be aware of any additional shimming requirements, and should communicate the requirements to the field crew. The Field Engineer/Specialist must communicate with the Application Engineer to obtain the correct amount of shims required for each tandem protector application.

Figure C-5: Maximus protector base with MaxJoint connection technology

<!-- image -->

## C.3.5.2 Tandem Maximus Protector Shimming Calculations

The amount of shims required between the upper and lower protector is calculated for each tandem protector application according to the well fluid temperature at pump setting depth (BHT), the lower protector make-up length and the material. Table C-5 provides the Maximus protector make-up length obtained from OneCAT, according to the series and number of chambers in the protectors. Verify this information in OneCat prior to installation.

Table C-5: Maximus Protectors Make-up Length

| Series      | 2 Chambers (in)   |   3 Chambers (in) |
|-------------|-------------------|-------------------|
| 375/325/375 | 68                |                96 |
| 387         | 70                |                96 |
| 400         | 70                |                96 |
| 540         | 78                |               107 |
| 562         | -                 |               108 |

The following are the formulas for calculating the amount of shims required between tandem Maximus protectors, according to the lower protector housing and shaft materials.

## Private

Equation C-1: Lower Protector with Carbon Steel housing and Monel shaft material

<!-- formula-not-decoded -->

Equation C-2: Lower Protector with Carbon Steel housing and Inconel shaft material

<!-- formula-not-decoded -->

Equation C-3: Lower Protector with Redalloy housing and Monel shaft material

<!-- formula-not-decoded -->

Equation C-4: Lower Protector with Redalloy housing and Inconel shaft material

<!-- formula-not-decoded -->

| Term   | Definition                                                           |
|--------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Shims  | Total thickness of shims (in)                                        |
| L      | Make-up length of lower protector (in)                               |
| BHT    | Well fluid temperature at pump setting depth (degF)                  |
| AT     | Ambient temperature (degF) at the manufacturing center. Use 75 degF. |

<!-- image -->

## Example

Conditions : Two 540-series protector are going to be installed in tandem. The lower protector has a two chamber configuration and is built using a Redalloy housing and Inconel shaft material. From Application Engineer information, the BHT of the well is 300 degF.

Question : What shim(s) should be added between the upper and lower protectors shaft?

Answer : From Table C-5: Maximus Protectors Make-up Length, the make-up length of a two chamber 540-series Protector is 78 in. By using Equation C-4: Lower Protector with Redalloy housing and Inconel shaft material, the shims required can be calculated as follows:

<!-- formula-not-decoded -->

Shims = One 1/16-in shim plate + Three 1/200-in shim plates ~ 0.0775 in

<!-- image -->

## Note

Convert the result of the shim calculation into fraction value (i.e., 1/16-in, 1/32-in, 1/64-in or 1/200-in) and use the shim plates provide in Table 4-23: Shim Material. Always round up the result from the calculation to maximum of 1/200 in (0.005 in).

## C.3.5.3 Installation Single or Lower Tandem Protector

<!-- image -->

Potential Severity:

Light

Potential Loss:

Information

Hazard Category:

Machinery equipment hand tools

Caution

Before proceeding, read and follow the general notes in section Appendix C.3.1: General Notes on MaxJoints and Shipping Caps.

1. Lift the protector to a position 2 to 3 ft above the motor.
2. Remove the shipping cap and gasket from the base of the protector.

## Private

3. Remove the O-ring and carefully install a new O-ring. The ALFORM-D connection tables (InTouch ID: 3255850) provide O-ring part numbers, coupling and bolt torque information.

<!-- image -->

## Note

A second backup O-ring is NOT required above the groove O-ring on 540and 562-series protectors.

4. Use spline wrenches to ensure the shafts of the motor and protector turn freely and smoothly.
5. Ensure the coupling is in place on the motor shaft.
6. Have the rig operator slowly lower the protector until the shafts are engaged.
- a. Turn the protector so that the flat cable slots on the protector flange and motor flange line up with each other.
- b. Lower the protector until the flanges meet, making sure not to damage the O-ring.
7. Insert the bolts and washers and torque them to specification.
8. Pick up the assembly by the protector clamp.
9. Remove the motor clamp
10. Lower the assembly until the protector clamp rests on the work table. While lowering the protector, inspect each drain-and-fill valve and vent plug for signs of leakage.
- a. Tighten the valve body to 35 lbf-ft.
- b. Tighten the vent plug in the valve to 15 lbf-ft.
11. Remove the compensating shipping cap from the protector head.
12. Using a spline wrench, check rotation of the assembly.
13. The protector is now ready for the installation of the next component of the string (e.g., intake, gas device, UT protector, or LT pump). Place a clean spare standard shipping cap on the head of the protector and tighten with two bolts to protect it from contamination while preparing the next string component.

## C.3.5.4 Installation of Upper Tandem Protector

<!-- image -->

## Note

375/325/375-series, 540-series and 562-series Maximus protectors do not have a UT or LT configuration. If these types of protectors are installed in tandem, the top (uppermost) protector will be called the UT and the bottom (lowermost) protector will be called the LT.

387-series UT and 400/400-series UT Maximus protectors have a 400-series flange at the base that can be connected directly to the head of any 400/456-series S/LT protector. 387-series and 400/400-series UT Maximus protectors come equipped with a tandem protector-to-protector coupling (P/N 0304444). No other couplings or adapters are required.

1. Lift the UT protector to a position 2 to 3 ft above the LT protector (or ProMotor throughout this section).
2. Remove the O-ring and carefully install a new O-ring. The ALFORM-D connection tables (InTouch ID: 3255850) provide O-ring part numbers, coupling and bolt torque information.

<!-- image -->

## Note

A second backup O-ring is NOT required above the groove O-ring on 540and 562-series protectors.

3. Use spline wrenches to ensure the shafts of the UT and LT protector turn freely and smoothly.
4. Ensure the coupling is in place on the S/LT protector shaft and place the required shims in the coupling of the S/LT protector. Refer to the following note.

<!-- image -->

## Note: Required shims

The required shims for Maximus tandem protectors are explained in section Appendix C.3.5: Protector Installation, while the formulas for calculating the required shims are available in section Appendix C.3.5.2: Tandem Maximus Protector Shimming Calculations.

## Private

5. Have the rig operator slowly lower the UT protector until the shafts are engaged.
- a. If a cable slot is present on the UT protector head or base, rotate the UT protector so that the cable slots line up with the LT protector or motor cable slot.
- b. Lower the protector until the flanges meet, making sure not to damage the O-ring.
6. Insert the bolts and washers and torque them to specification.
7. Pick up the assembly by the UT protector clamp.
8. Remove the LT protector clamp and lower the assembly until the UT protector clamp rests on the work table. While lowering the UT protector, inspect each drain-and-fill valve and vent plug for signs of leakage.
- a. Tighten the valve body to 35 lbf-ft.
- b. Tighten the vent plug in the valve to 15 lbf-ft.
9. Remove the compensating shipping cap from the UT protector head. Using a spline wrench, check rotation of the assembly.
10. The protector is now ready for the installation of the next component of the string (e.g., intake, gas device, or pump). Place a clean spare standard shipping cap on the head of the protector and tighten with two bolts to protect it from contamination while preparing the next string component.

## C.3.6 Shimming Procedures for Protectors-to-Pumps

Maximus protectors include the factory shimming feature and should be installed accordingly. Refer to the pump shimming and installation procedures in the Wellsite Procedures section.

## C.3.7 MaxLok Plug-in Pothead Installation

The MaxLok ESP motor pothead design eliminates the need for taping pothead electrical connections considerably reducing the time required to make the connection while maintaining the same performance and reliability.

<!-- image -->

Figure C-6: Maximus Motor Lead Extension (MLE) with MaxLok motor pothead

<!-- image -->

Potential Severity:

Light

Potential Loss:

Assets

Hazard Category:

Machinery equipment hand tools

Caution

Do not install a non-Maximus plug-in MLE/pothead into a Maximus motor. This combination will not seal properly and a failure will, likely, result. All Maximus MLEs/potheads must be checked prior to installation to confirm that they are compatible with Maximus motor.

The Maximus pothead seals with a O-ring contained on a groove, as shown in the figure Figure C-6. Non-Maximus potheads utilize a 'trap' seal and do not have an O-ring groove. The two are NOT interchangeable and cannot be mixed

Equipment tests and assembly procedures for the plug-in design are similar to tests and procedures for the standard plug-in design.

Raise the string until the pothole on the UT or S motor (or UT or S ProMotor) is at a comfortable working height.

1. While holding the pothole shipping cover down, remove the nuts.
2. Remove the shipping cover.
3. Remove the shipping cap from the flat cable extension.
4. Remove the O-ring.
5. Apply a coating of Dow #4 or Dow #111 grease to a new O-ring. Install the O-ring in the pothead O-ring gland.

6. Inspect the inside of the pothead flange to verify that a black rubber gasket is installed. The light gray color of the pothead front terminal block will be observed if a gasket is not installed.

<!-- image -->

## Note

If a gasket is found in the shipping cap rather than installed in the pothead:

- a. Ensure the gasket is clean and undamaged.
- b. Apply a coating of Dow #4 or Dow#111 grease to the gasket.
- c. Push the gasket into the pothead cavity. It will be pushed into the proper location when the pothead is plugged to the motor terminal block.

<!-- image -->

Potential Severity:

Light

Potential Loss:

Assets

Hazard Category:

Machinery equipment hand tools

Caution

Do not install two gaskets. The installation of two gaskets may crack the terminal block. This will result in insufficient terminal engagement, a short to ground and disassembly problems when the pothead is unplugged from the motor.

<!-- image -->

Potential Severity:

Light

Potential Loss:

Assets, Reputation

Hazard Category:

Electrical

Caution

Ensure the PEEK shroud external surface is free from moisture, condensation and contamination. This surface is sensitive to arc tracking and must be protected by motor oil or silicon grease.

7. Fill the remaining pothead cavity with Dow #4 grease or Reda #5 motor oil.

- Motor oil: Flood the pothole and the pothead front cavity with Reda #5 motor oil or apply a coating of Dow #4 or Dow #111 to the front cavity of the pothead.

<!-- image -->

Potential Severity:

Light

Potential Loss:

Assets

Hazard Category:

Machinery equipment hand tools, Temperature

Caution

Do not use grease in temperatures below 5 degF (-15 degC). Instead, flush the pothead and pothole with the proper motor oil immediately before plugging-in. In cold weather, the grease can be so stiff that it interferes with electrical contact.

- Grease: Fill the front cavity of the pothead evenly with Dow #4 or Dow #11 grease. The small gaps between the PEEK shroud/flange and between the three PEEK shrouds must be filled with the grease. Displace as much air as possible from the pothead cavity with the grease.

<!-- image -->

Arc path

Figure C-7: Fill Pothead Cavity. Fill the cavity with Reda #5 motor oil or coat with Dow #4 or Dow #111 grease.

8. Ensure that no moisture or contamination has been introduced to the pothead.
9. Align the terminals, then quickly and carefully push the pothead assembly into the motor pothole by hand.
10. Hold the pothead in position and install the retaining nuts.
11. Tighten the retaining nuts down evenly and torque to 16 lbf-ft.

## Private

<!-- image -->

Potential Severity:

Light

Potential Loss:

Assets

Hazard Category:

Machinery equipment hand tools

Caution

The pothole is equipped with a valve that prevents oil loss while the pothole is open, but allows pressure equalization when the pothead is attached. While pothead is half engaged, oil can seep out, so the pothead should be plugged in quickly to minimize oil loss. Hold the pothead fully engaged while installing or removing the nuts but do not leave the pothead half engaged. Loss of a few spoonfuls of oil would not be a problem, but if a cupful was lost, the protector should be refilled per the standard oil filling procedures for protectors like a Modular protector.

The string is now ready for electrical testing through the cable, tubing installation and cable banding per the standard cable testing procedures and wellsite procedures.

## C.3.8 Trident Plug-in Pothead Installation

Currently, there are two types of Trident MLE are available: Trident-300 and Trident-400. The Trident-300 is used with the 738 Maximus motor for off-shore applications and has pothead pressure test ports on the motor head. The Trident-400 is used with the 562 High Ampacity Maximus motor and does not have pressure test ports.

The Trident-300 pothead and Trident-400 pothead have identical geometry and dimensions. The only differences between the two potheads are the O-ring materials and configurations. The Trident-300 pothead uses two size 2-022, HNBR, 70 Durometer O-rings. The Trident-400 pothead uses one size 2-022, Low Temperature 75 Durometer O-ring and one PEEK gland filling ring. This is because 562 Maximus motor head does not have pressure test ports.

1. Install UT motor with Trident motohead. Refer to Appendix C.3.4.4: Installation of UT Motor with Trident Motor Head.
2. Perform UT motor electrical checks.
- a. Remove the three pothole caps from the UT motor, visually inspect internal electrical connections.

## Private

Figure C-8: Maximus Trident motor head

<!-- image -->

- b. Install special UT motor test probes (P/N 101049527) into the motor head potholes.

<!-- image -->

Figure C-9: Test Motor using Trident Test Probes

<!-- image -->

## Note

The Trident test probes allow the testing of the UT motor and reduce the risk of contamination during testing. Record all electrical data on ESP system integrity sheet.

- c. Perform ground resistance tests.
- d. Perform phase resistance tests.
- e. Perform functional tests on downhole gauge.
3. Remove electrical test probes and replace the pothole caps.

## Private

4. Perform UT motor mechanical checks.
- a. Verify that the flange and seal face are not damaged.
- b. Ensure the coupling part number is checked against the power string number and installed correctly on the motor shaft.
- c. Check motor shaft rotation using special tools (100835923).
- d. Align UT motor shaft for matching procedure using special tool (100831872).
- e. Service the UT motor head using fresh dielectric oil.
- f. Cover and protect UT motor head in preparation to install the LT protector.
5. Install the LT protector.

<!-- image -->

## Note

The Trident MLE must be installed after the installation of LT protector and before the installation of the tandem protector. This prevents the hydrostatic force of the motor oil in the protector from forcing the motor oil out of the trident potholes when the pothole caps are removed. Also, the MLE will cause problems if the LT protector is installed to the motor after the MLE.

6. Prepare the Trident MLE for installation.
- a. Pull the MLE from the reel and temporarily secured the MLE above motor head.
- b. Identify the phase sequence A-B-C on pothead.

<!-- image -->

## Note

Phase sequence should be A-B-C from left to right.

- c. Separate the MLE, allow enough separation and flexibility while preparing the pothead.
- d. Check the hard stamp A-B-C mark, from left to right, on the potholes of the motor head.
- e. Remove pothead shipping caps and visually check for any damage on sealing surfaces and terminals.

## Private

<!-- image -->

Potential Severity:

Light

Potential Loss:

Assets

Hazard Category:

Machinery equipment hand tools

Caution

Always keep the shipping cap closed unless the pothead is being tested or installed. The terminal insulator (shroud) of the pothead is very sensitive to moisture and contamination. NEVER contact the shroud with dirty hands.

7. Remove and discard original O-rings installed on the pothead for shipping purpose.
8. Install the supplied new O-rings into the O-ring grooves.
- a. Trident-300 pothead : Install two new size 2-022 HNBR O-rings (100781769) into the two O-ring grooves on each pothead.
- b. Trident-400 pothead : Install one new size 2-022 Viton O-ring (100925883) into the small O-ring groove on the lower end of each pothead. Verify a PEEK gland filling ring (with scuff cut) has been installed in the larger O-ring groove on the upper end of each pothead. It is factory installed to prevent the installation of an O-ring in this groove by mistake. Do NOT install an O-ring in this groove.

Figure C-10: Trident-300 pothead

<!-- image -->

The Trident-300 potheads only use size 2-022 O-rings, HNBR 70 Durometer (100781769). The Trident-400 potheads only use size 2-022 O-rings, 75 Durometer, GT 761 (100925883). Do not use any O-rings made from other materials, or by any other suppliers.

9. Apply a small amount of Dow Corning 111 grease onto the O-ring surfaces.
10. Verify that the pothead terminals and surrounding area are clean for the electrical connection.
11. Insert each Trident pothead into the motor head and hand-tighten the pothead retaining nut (Figure C-12: Trident Pothead Connections).

## Note

Make sure O-rings are fully engaged. Be careful not damage the O-rings while installing the potheads in the potholes.

12. Tighten each 1-3/16-in pothead retaining nut to specified torque 35 ft-lbf with the pre-set torque wrench (100793643).
13. Verify that all three pothead connections are installed correctly.
14. Pothead installation is complete.

## Note: Pressure test Trident-300 pothead

Each Trident-300 pothead connection must be pressure tested before continuing to the next step. Refer to Appendix C.3.8.1: Trident-300 Pressure Test for pressure test procedure.

The Trident-400 pothead connections are not pressure tested. The 562 Maximus motor head does not have pressure test ports.

15. The string is now ready for electrical testing through the cable, tubing installation, and cable banding per the standard wellsite procedures.

## C.3.8.1 Trident-300 Pressure Test

Each Trident-300 pothead connection must be pressure tested using the pressure test ports on the motor head.

1. Install the pressure test manifold to the SAE port in the UT motor head.
2. Connect hydraulic pump to the pressure test manifold. Pump and bleed the hose from pump to manifold before connecting.
3. Pressure up to 100 psi; stabilize pressure and hold for 5 minutes.

Figure C-14: Pressure Test Trident Pothead Connection

<!-- image -->

<!-- image -->

## Note

Do not over pressurize the gauge. Ensure you have a good view of the gauge as it is very easy to over pressurize the gauge and damage it.

4. Record the pressure after 5 minutes.
5. Lower pressure to 10 psi; stabilize pressure and hold for another 5 minutes.
6. Record the pressure after 5 minutes.
7. If the Trident pothead successfully passed the pressure test, continue to next step.

If the pothead failed the pressure test,

- a. Remove the pothead from the motor head.
- b. Thoroughly check and analyze the causes of the failure, and solve problems.
- c. Reinstall pothead and pressure test the pothead connection again. Repeat steps 8 through 13 in the section Appendix C.3.8: Trident Plug-in Pothead Installation.
8. After a successful pressure test, remove the manifold and equipment and replace the SAE plugs.

<!-- image -->

## Note

Do NOT install O-rings on the SAE plugs. Verify that the plug (100813229) has a groove on the internal face that allows a communication path. This will ensure that the pressure will not build between the O-rings during the operation.

9. The string is now ready for electrical testing through the cable, tubing installation, and cable banding per the standard wellsite procedures.
